record.original_question: Suppose n >= 2 and Lambda is a lattice in R^(n+1) with positive homogeneous minimum N(Lambda) > 0, where N(Lambda) is the infimum of |z_0 z_1 ... z_n| over nonzero lattice points z = (z_0, ..., z_n). Must every such lattice be algebraic?

evidence.quote: For an arbitrary lattice Λ ⊂ Rn+1 we consider its homogeneous minima N (Λ) = inf |z0 z1 · · · zn |.
A famous Oppenheim conjecture supposes that in the case n ⩾ 2 any lattice Λ satisfying N (L) > 0 is an algebraic lattice. This conjecture is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2 be an integer. For a full-rank lattice Λ ⊂ ℝ^{n+1}, define its homogeneous minimum by
   N(Λ) = inf { |z_0 z_1 ⋯ z_n| : z = (z_0, z_1, …, z_n) ∈ Λ, z ≠ 0 }.
A lattice Λ ⊂ ℝ^{n+1} is called algebraic if there exists a totally real algebraic number field K of degree n+1 over ℚ with real embeddings σ_0, …, σ_n, a fractional ideal (or, more generally, a full ℤ-module) M ⊂ K of rank n+1, and a nonzero real scalar c such that
   Λ = c · { (σ_0(α), σ_1(α), …, σ_n(α)) : α ∈ M }.
Equivalently, Λ is algebraic if it is, up to scaling and the natural action of the diagonal group, commensurable with the image of the ring of integers of a totally real number field of degree n+1 under its embedding into ℝ^{n+1} via the n+1 real places.

Question: Must every lattice Λ ⊂ ℝ^{n+1} with N(Λ) > 0 be algebraic?
artifact.category_tag: Oppenheim conjecture on products of linear forms
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (a variant of Oppenheim's conjecture on products of n+1 linear forms, due to Cassels–Swinnerton-Dyer and related to Littlewood's conjecture) remains open. Margulis's celebrated 1987 theorem resolved the quadratic-form version, but the product-of-linear-forms version asserting that any lattice with positive homogeneous minimum must be algebraic is still unresolved; it is known to imply Littlewood's conjecture in the n=2 case.

status_evidence.title: Oppenheim conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Margulis proved the Oppenheim conjecture on quadratic forms in 1987.
status_evidence.claim: The classical (quadratic-form) Oppenheim conjecture is solved, but the product-of-linear-forms variant is distinct.

status_evidence.title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation

status_evidence.claim: The lattice/algebraicity version of the Oppenheim conjecture is reported as open.
